newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Lebanon buys dollars - Governor.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Lebanon buys dollars - Governor.

text.p: The Bank of Lebanon has bought more than $900 million on the Beirut foreign exchange market since the start of 1997, Governor Riad Salameh said on Wednesday.
"The Bank of Lebanon has intervened as a buyer of more than $900 million since the beginning of the year," Salameh told Arab bankers and financiers at a conference in Beirut.
The rate of dolarisation of bank deposits fell to 55 percent in April, he added.
Foreign exchange dealers told Reuters the central bank had consistently bought dollars on the market this year.
"There have only been about 20 days on which the Bank of Lebanon did not take dollars from the market," Talal Abou Zaki, forex manager at Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, said.

"There are still people offering dollars and switching to Lebanese pounds, and I think there are also outside investors taking advantage of high interest rates on the Lebanese pound who are buying treasury bills," Abou Zaki said.
The Lebanese pound has continued its steady appreciation against the U.S. dollar during 1997.
It is currently at 1,542.5 to the dollar compared with 1,552 at the end of December 1996.
